title: Irreducibility of an affine spectrum is equivalent to primality of the nilradical
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring. Write $N_R=\{x\in R: x^n=0\text{ for some integer }n\geq1\}$ for its nilradical ideal. Then $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] if and only if $N_R$ is a prime ideal: $N_R\ne R$ and, for every $a,b\in R$, $ab\in N_R$ implies $a\in N_R$ or $b\in N_R$. In particular irreducibility includes nonemptiness, and the zero ring does not satisfy either side.

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, assertion (2) and its proof, applied to the radical of the zero ideal: $V(0)=V(N_R)=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The radical-ideal/closed-set identification used in that proof identifies the unique prime defining the whole spectrum with $N_R$.
